Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

doctor — a person who treats ill people. Example: The doctor says I should rest.
headache — a pain in your head. Example: I have got a headache.
fever — a body temperature that is too high. Example: She has got a fever.
cough — a sudden noise from your chest when ill. Example: I have got a bad cough.
medicine — something you take when you are ill. Example: Take this medicine twice a day.
rest — to stop working and relax. Example: You should rest.
water — the clear liquid we drink. Example: I drink a lot of water.
sleep — to rest with your eyes closed at night. Example: I sleep eight hours.
pain — a feeling that something hurts. Example: The pain is in my head.
advice — an opinion about what you should do. Example: That is good advice.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• You should rest.
• You shouldn't work.
• You should drink water.
• Should I take the medicine?
• That is good advice.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
The doctor gives me advice. I have got a headache and a fever. I should rest and drink water. I shouldn't work this week. I should take the medicine twice a day.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: What should I do? B: You should rest and drink water. A: Should I take the medicine? B: Yes, twice a day. And you shouldn't work.

• You should drink water.
